$comment: 🛍️ The app-static catalogue is fetched ONCE PER APP INSTANCE. This fixture pins the rule on the failure path, where it used to be dropped: the shell recorded the instance only after a successful reassembly, so a catalogue that failed was re-fetched by every later refresh — and a refresh runs on every settled command. The second fetch of `framework.section.catalogue` never returned from its own turn, so `boot_shell` never returned either and the canvas never bound a pointer listener. Language-agnostic: `expectedFetchIndices` is what the rule must produce, `baselineFetchIndices` is what recording-only-successes produced, and a case where they differ is a case this fixture discriminates.

rule.statement: A refresh claims the fetch when the recorded instance differs from the refresh's instance; claiming records the instance immediately, before the fetch runs, so the outcome of that fetch can never change how many fetches happen.

cases.name: a-catalogue-that-reassembles-is-fetched-once
cases.why: The unbroken path, unchanged by the fix — five refreshes of one instance, one fetch.

cases.name: a-catalogue-whose-reassembly-fails-is-still-fetched-once
cases.why: The defect. The live target's own boot: the first fetch published a document whose payload did not reassemble, and every later refresh re-entered the fetch. The second one wedged boot.

cases.name: a-catalogue-whose-fetch-faults-is-still-fetched-once
cases.why: The other failure arm — `render_with_document` itself errors — must claim the attempt exactly as the reassembly arm does.

cases.name: a-new-app-instance-refetches-exactly-once
cases.why: The cache key is the instance, so switching session must refetch — the fix must not turn 'once per instance' into 'once per process'.

cases.name: a-new-instance-refetches-once-even-after-a-failure
cases.why: A failed instance must not poison the next one, and must not earn the next one a second attempt either.
